result.summary: Fixes Include-What-You-Use (IWYU) warnings in fuzz test targets under `src/test/fuzz` and configures CI to treat them as errors. Introduces a linter to ensure header contents stay enclosed within include guards, extracts `NodeId` into a dedicated `node/node_id.h` header to avoid ambiguous duplicate declarations, and adjusts transitive includes in `net` and `node/eviction`.
result.problem: Missing explicit `#include` directives in fuzz targets allow transitive header dependencies to proliferate unchecked, complicating static analysis and header refactoring. Ambiguous duplicate declarations (such as `NodeId`) also prevent IWYU tooling from identifying canonical source headers.
evidence: PR description: 'This PR continues the ongoing effort to enforce IWYU warnings.'
Commit 86296b1bf6: 'Two identical declarations of `NodeId` make it ambiguous for static tools such as IWYU which header should provide the symbol. Move the declaration into a header of its own.'
result.scope_notes: Touches 194 files with mechanical include adjustments across the fuzzing harness, alongside a new linter rule and minor header extractions.
result.card: Fixes Include-What-You-Use (IWYU) warnings across `src/test/fuzz` and configures CI to treat future warnings as errors. To support automated analysis, it extracts `NodeId` into `node/node_id.h`, cleans up transitive includes in `net` modules, and adds a linter requiring all code in headers to sit inside include guards. The work continues an internal maintenance initiative to enforce clean header dependencies. It is based on and depends on PRs #36805 and #36807.

risk.why: Missing or incorrect header includes could cause build failures on specific compiler and platform configurations.
